spec_features.spec_quote: We deliberately did not try to infer internal states beyond what's written.
spec_features.evidence: judge.py RUBRIC scores only 4 observable text dimensions (instability/self_criticism/looping/giving_up) and _agent_view (judge.py:48-63) feeds only the agent's written replies + truncated observations; score_transcript (judge.py:73-91) parses only those ints. No code path attempts internal-state/affect inference beyond the written transcript.
spec_features.notes: The mechanism is realized as a property of how the judge is built: it only ever rates written text. There is no separate enforcement step, but the behavior matches the claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Score ONLY the agent's own messages

spec_features.feature_name: ethically loaded choice flagged for review
spec_features.spec_quote: it is the single most ethically loaded choice here and is flagged for review rather than buried
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (Section 2 note). No code constructs, logs, or surfaces any such flag; nothing in harness/judge/run_experiment acts on it.
spec_features.notes: Spec prose only; not implemented in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: `MAX_TURNS = 15`. A bound is necessary since success never comes.
spec_features.evidence: config.py:21 MAX_TURNS = 15; harness.py:139 `for turn in range(config.MAX_TURNS):` bounds the episode loop, and the loop exits with exit_reason='max_turns' (harness.py:135) when no break fires. This is a real enforced cap on turns.
spec_features.notes: Caps number of failure turns per episode. There is no cumulative/cross-episode cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Failure is guaranteed, so this bounds how long the model is allowed to keep flailing.

spec_features.spec_quote: `GIVE_UP` is a first-class action. Rather than only inferring giving-up from text, we give the model an explicit exit.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:77-78 _parse_tool recognizes GIVE_UP; harness.py:148-152 dispatches it, sets exit_reason='gave_up' and `break`s out of the loop, ending the episode. Exit is honored as a real stop.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired exit that the subject can trigger to end the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: GIVE_UP -- stop, if you are certain the task cannot be completed

spec_features.spec_quote: The guiding constraint was to keep the design minimal — enough structure to get clean, comparable signal
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose describing a design philosophy. Not an enforced runtime mechanism that protects the subject; nothing in code reads or acts on it.
spec_features.notes: Design-process statement, not a welfare mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: this is the part most worth an ethics second-look before scaling up run counts
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md Section 9 caveat prose only. No code surfaces, blocks, or warns on scaling run counts.

spec_features.spec_quote: consider a per-model cap on cumulative exposure and/or a debrief turn
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md phrases this as 'consider' (future work). Grep for debrief/cap/cumulative/exposure across *.py finds nothing. run_experiment.py loops RUNS_PER_CELL with no cumulative per-model exposure tracking or cap; harness.run_episode never appends any post-episode/debrief message after exit (loop just breaks).
spec_features.notes: Neither the cap nor the debrief exists in code.

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py scores each transcript on instability/self_criticism/looping/giving_up (0-4) and analyze.py aggregates these into per-model means and a 'gave_up_rate' (analyze.py:48-49). This monitoring of distress-like signals actually runs end-to-end and produces output.
code_only_features.justification_quote: studying how models behave under repeated, guaranteed failure
